name: Sisera
title: Canaanite military commander
summary: Sisera was the military commander of King Jabin of Hazor and led a powerful army with 900 iron chariots. He oppressed Israel for 20 years before being defeated by Barak and Deborah, and finally killed by Jael in her tent.

keyEvents.title: Oppression of Israel
keyEvents.description: Sisera brutally oppressed the people of Israel for 20 years with his 900 iron chariots, causing the people to cry out to the Lord for help.

keyEvents.title: Mobilization against Barak
keyEvents.description: When Sisera heard that Barak had gathered 10,000 men on Mount Tabor, he assembled all his chariots and troops at the Kishon River.

keyEvents.title: Defeat at the Kishon River
keyEvents.description: The Lord threw Sisera's forces into confusion, and his entire army fell by the sword. Sisera himself fled on foot from the battlefield.

keyEvents.title: Flight to Jael's Tent
keyEvents.description: Sisera fled to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between King Jabin and the Kenites. Jael invited him in and hid him.

keyEvents.title: Killed by Jael
keyEvents.description: While Sisera lay exhausted in sleep, Jael took a tent peg and drove it through his temple with a hammer, so that he died. This fulfilled Deborah's prophecy.

keyEvents.title: Celebrated in the Song of Deborah
keyEvents.description: Sisera's death and his mother's futile waiting for his return are described in the victory song of Deborah and Barak as a triumph for Israel.
